title: Zarr, NetCDF4, and geospatial HDF5 client maturity boundary

references.assertion: Authenticated v1 admin CRUD and asynchronous refresh/status routes exist for multidimensional coverage registrations.
The server domain names CloudOptimizedHdf5, NetCdf4, and Grib registration formats and variable/dimension metadata records.
Registration validates cloud provider, object path, extension, and bounded declared variable names without proving readable bytes.
ADR-0039 selects GDAL sidecar conversion to derived Zarr and explicitly rejects a browser or in-process whole-file reader path.
The refresh path dispatches an internal native-profile metadata job and can best-effort register its derived Zarr output.
The optional native worker runs gdalmdiminfo and best-effort gdal_translate to Zarr through bounded VSI access.
The pinned ubuntu-full worker build checks netCDF and GRIB drivers, but contains no explicit HDF5 driver assertion or deployed-image receipt.
Server tests exercise admin registration and job dispatch with in-memory doubles, not a pinned live NetCDF or HDF5 object and worker.
Worker tests verify command construction, artifact mapping, path handling, and failure behavior with fake command results rather than live format bytes.
The default managed multidimensional reader advertises no supported formats and throws a stable reader-unavailable error.
Maps versioned Zarr administration and public datacube tile routes.
Exercises register, list, get, and delete lifecycle operations through HTTP without proving a readable public store.
Registers Zarr services in the server composition root.
Binds registered Zarr stores to OGC API Coverages and plans bounded CoverageJSON subsets.
Proves chunk-aware bounded subset reads with deterministic in-memory fixtures.
Proves the datacube HTTP route exists, but only records the no-registration negative path.
Records datacube route coverage plus planner and renderer component evidence.
Exercises positive registered-Zarr native-CRS PNG slices and explicit unsupported cases through HTTP fixtures.

policy.unblockRule: A focused experimental Zarr server client may ship against the versioned registration, metadata, and tile contract; direct Zarr reads and every NetCDF4/HDF5 client remain gated on their listed fixtures, runtime proof, bounded interfaces, and deployment evidence.

trackedFormats.label: NetCDF-4
trackedFormats.scopeBoundary: CF-aware NetCDF-4 coverage variables, dimensions, coordinates, attributes, grids, chunks, scale/offset, calendars, vertical axes, and no-data; never an implicit whole-file browser download.

evidence.statement: The server has authenticated v1 admin registration CRUD for NetCdf4 objects; registration is catalog metadata, not readable client data.
A separately deployed native worker can scan NetCDF metadata and best-effort convert the object to derived Zarr; this is not guaranteed in every server build or deployment.
No pinned public versioned HTTP contract proves client inspection of NetCDF variables, dimensions, coordinates, attributes, or conventions.
No pinned public versioned HTTP contract proves bounded NetCDF variable, time, vertical, or spatial subsetting with explicit limits.
The pinned native worker Dockerfile checks for a netCDF GDAL driver at image build time, but no deployed image matrix or runtime receipt is pinned here.
No immutable public or CI NetCDF fixture is bound to a real Honua registration, worker conversion, derived Zarr, and bounded result receipt.
No scheduled canary proves NetCDF registration through bounded read across a deployed server and worker version pair.
The JavaScript SDK intentionally exposes no NetCDF adapter, types, error surface, package export, or runnable example.

client.summary: The JavaScript SDK exposes no NetCDF adapter, public types, request operations, or package entrypoint.

server.summary: Authenticated registration and build-optional metadata scanning exist, but no stable public variable or bounded subset read contract is proven.

endToEnd.summary: No deployed server-to-JavaScript path proves bounded NetCDF inspection or subset semantics.

trackedFormats.label: Geospatial HDF5
trackedFormats.scopeBoundary: Only HDF5 datasets that map to a documented geospatial coverage model; generic group browsing and an implication that arbitrary HDF5 is spatial are explicitly outside scope.

evidence.statement: The server has authenticated v1 admin registration CRUD for CloudOptimizedHdf5 objects; registration does not establish CF mapping or readable bytes.
ADR-0039 routes HDF5 through the optional GDAL worker and derived Zarr, while the managed default reader remains disabled.
No pinned public versioned HTTP contract proves geospatial HDF5 dataset/group, variable, dimension, coordinate, attribute, or convention inspection.
No pinned public versioned HTTP contract proves bounded geospatial HDF5 variable, time, vertical, or spatial subset reads.
The worker image commentary expects HDF support, but its executable build guard checks netCDF and GRIB only and no HDF5 driver/runtime matrix is pinned.
No immutable geospatial HDF5 fixture is bound to a real Honua registration, worker conversion, derived Zarr, and bounded result receipt.
No scheduled canary proves geospatial HDF5 registration through bounded read across a deployed server and worker version pair.
The JavaScript SDK intentionally exposes no HDF5 adapter, types, error surface, package export, generic group browser, or runnable example.

client.summary: The JavaScript SDK exposes no geospatial HDF5 adapter, public types, request operations, or package entrypoint.

server.summary: Authenticated registration and build-optional conversion architecture exist, but HDF5 driver and public bounded-read proof are missing.

endToEnd.summary: No deployed server-to-JavaScript path proves geospatial HDF5 inspection or bounded subset semantics.

trackedFormats.label: Zarr v2 / v3
trackedFormats.scopeBoundary: Read-only, bounded Zarr v2 and v3 metadata, subset, CoverageJSON, WCS, and datacube tile paths with explicit codec, layout, coordinate, CRS, and resource limits; no Zarr authoring, unrestricted enumeration, or implicit browser full-store download.

client.summary: The JavaScript SDK exposes a versioned registration and metadata client plus a byte-bounded server tile handoff; direct object-store and general slice reads remain unavailable.

server.summary: Registration, bounded subset internals, CoverageJSON, WCS fixtures, and datacube route components exist without a positive public live canary.

endToEnd.summary: No public deployment and JavaScript client jointly prove the pinned Zarr contract, budgets, errors, and rendering handoff.

evidence.statement: Versioned Zarr admin registration CRUD and refresh routes are composed and exercised through HTTP lifecycle tests.
evidence.route: POST /api/v1/admin/zarr-stores with list, get, delete, and refresh operations
evidence.boundary: The lifecycle test does not prove a readable public object-store fixture or a successful metadata refresh.

evidence.statement: Server components parse bounded Zarr v2 and v3 metadata for registered stores, but no stable public metadata inspection contract is pinned.
evidence.route: Registered-store metadata behind OGC API Coverages services
evidence.boundary: Component evidence does not establish general store enumeration, consolidated metadata support, or a public versioned client contract.

evidence.statement: Chunk-aware bounded subset reads and CoverageJSON planning exist with hard limits, but positive public HTTP proof is absent.
evidence.boundary: Reader fixtures and service components do not replace a Zarr-specific positive deployed coverage receipt.

evidence.statement: ZarrCoverageService maps registered stores to collection, schema, and bounded CoverageJSON responses.
evidence.boundary: No Zarr-specific positive OGC API Coverages HTTP round trip or public live response is pinned.

evidence.statement: The public datacube route, planner, and PNG renderer components are evidenced for registered Zarr slices.
evidence.boundary: The endpoint test is negative-path only and does not prove a positive registered-store HTTP or live tile response.

evidence.statement: WCS 2.0.1 fixtures return bounded native-CRS PNG slices for registered Zarr data and exercise explicit failures.
evidence.route: WCS 2.0.1 GetCoverage through ImageServer and service routes
evidence.boundary: TIFF and range-subset composition remain unsupported and no public live WCS receipt is pinned.

evidence.statement: The audited implementation has explicit v2/v3, codec, chunk layout, coordinate, CRS, and resource-budget boundaries.
evidence.route: Internal Zarr metadata and chunk readers used by coverage and tile services
evidence.boundary: The implementation matrix is not yet backed by immutable public v2/v3 fixtures and deterministic range traces.

evidence.statement: No immutable redistributable Zarr v2 and v3 fixtures are bound to expected metadata, subset, tile, and range-trace digests.
No scheduled public canary proves advertised Zarr coverage and datacube routes against a pinned deployment.
The JavaScript SDK exposes experimental registration and metadata operations, explicit maturity failures, and a byte-bounded server tile handoff with focused unit tests.

versions: Zarr v2 reads .zgroup, .zattrs, and .zarray; grouped discovery depends on an optional attributes variables manifest.
Zarr v3 reads root and child zarr.json nodes; grouped discovery depends on the root attributes variables list and is not general store enumeration.
codecs: Tested reads cover v2 uncompressed and zlib chunks plus v3 uncompressed and gzip chunks.
Zarr v3 zstd, blosc, sharding_indexed, crc32c, and unknown codecs are rejected.
Filters, Fortran order, big-endian values, and unsupported non-numeric data types are rejected.
layout: C-order regular chunk grids are supported, including v3 c-prefixed and v2-style dotted chunk keys.
Coordinates depend on Honua variable, dimension, extent, and CRS attributes rather than unrestricted CF/Zarr inference.
crs: Server georeferencing reads Honua crs_wkid and extent attributes when present.
Datacube tile requests require the tile matrix set SRID to equal the coverage storage SRID.
Cross-CRS reprojection of a Zarr tile window is not implemented.
budgets: Metadata documents are capped at 64 KiB and discovery is capped at 64 variables.
The subset reader caps a request at 4096 chunks and 256 MiB decoded data.
OGC API Coverage output is capped at 16 MiB decoded data and a datacube tile slice at 4 MiB decoded data.

publicationGates.requirement: Publish a redistributable immutable fixture URL, license, SHA-256 digest, expected metadata, subset digest, and tile digest.
Cover one supported Zarr v2 store and one supported Zarr v3 store across codec, CRS, spatial, temporal, vertical, and named dimensions.
Record deterministic byte-range traces proving chunk-bounded reads and rejection at declared request limits.
Record a deployed server commit and capability manifest that advertise the exact Zarr-backed routes under test.
Fetch a bounded public Zarr-backed OGC API Coverage subset and verify media type, byte limit, axes, shape, and digest.
Fetch a public Zarr-backed datacube PNG tile and verify media type, dimensions, byte limit, and digest.
Pin a versioned server contract for registration, metadata, subset, tile, version, codec, coordinate, CRS, and errors.
Implement typed metadata, slice, and tile operations with byte and chunk budgets, cancellation, auth, interception, and typed errors.
Pass deterministic fixture contracts and scheduled live evidence without adding unsupported codecs or coordinate inference.
Publish a runnable sample only after the SDK export exists and both fixture and live evidence gates pass.

futureResponsibilities.statement: Describe groups, arrays, dimensions, chunks, data types, codecs, fill values, coordinates, CRS, and consolidated metadata without array payload downloads.
Read an explicitly bounded spatial, temporal, vertical, or named-dimension slice through chunk-aware requests.
Request a bounded server datacube tile or adapt an admitted two-dimensional slice without hiding CRS or resampling limits.

crossCutting: Cancellation and authentication must flow through the shared request pipeline.
Request interception must expose every metadata, range, subset, and tile request.
Byte, chunk, dimension, and decoded-output budgets must default closed and remain observable.
Unsupported versions, codecs, coordinates, and CRS transformations must fail with typed errors.
Direct object-store access and Honua server operations must remain distinct execution modes.

referenceOnlyFormats.label: GRIB / GRIB2
referenceOnlyFormats.statement: Server source includes a Grib registration enum, extension validation, conversion-path test reference, and GDAL image guard. GRIB is outside issue #1121 and creates no SDK roadmap, support claim, or curriculum lane here.

releaseBlockers.requirement: Publish bounded variable, spatial, temporal, and vertical subset operations without whole-file fallback.
releaseBlockers.evidenceNeeded: Positive and limit-rejection contract tests covering range, byte, cell, variable, and timeout budgets.

releaseBlockers.requirement: Pin an explicit NetCDF4 and HDF5 GDAL driver/image/version matrix for every supported deployment profile.
releaseBlockers.evidenceNeeded: Image build assertions plus deployed runtime receipts for each claimed format and architecture.

releaseBlockers.requirement: Bind immutable, license-safe fixtures with known variables, dimensions, coordinates, chunks, fill values, and expected subset digests.
releaseBlockers.evidenceNeeded: Fixture hashes, registration receipt, conversion artifact digest, and deterministic bounded response assertions.

releaseBlockers.requirement: Continuously prove the complete server and native-worker path against pinned deployed versions.
releaseBlockers.evidenceNeeded: Scheduled redacted canary receipts covering metadata, bounded subsets, cancellation, auth, failures, and derived-artifact provenance.

releaseBlockers.requirement: Design the client only after server proof, with bounded requests, typed metadata/errors, cancellation, auth, interceptors, cache rules, and safe render/columnar handoffs.

releaseBlockers.requirement: Publish immutable Zarr v2 and v3 fixtures covering supported codecs, layouts, dimensions, coordinates, CRS, and expected results.

releaseBlockers.requirement: Prove advertised Zarr-backed CoverageJSON, WCS, and datacube tile routes against a pinned public deployment.
releaseBlockers.evidenceNeeded: Capability manifest, server commit, request receipts, media types, axes, shapes, dimensions, byte ceilings, and output digests.

releaseBlockers.requirement: Stabilize public metadata, subset, tile, version, codec, layout, coordinate, CRS, error, and request-budget semantics.
releaseBlockers.evidenceNeeded: Generated server contract documentation plus positive and limit-rejection tests for every admitted version and codec lane.

releaseBlockers.requirement: Implement reviewed metadata, slice, and tile operations with typed errors and closed resource budgets.
